species: Tightly synchronised, ring-stage ACβ-HA:loxP or PKAc-HA:loxP parasites were treated with 100 nM RAP or vehicle only (DMSO) and schizonts (about 45 h old) enriched on an approximately 70% Percoll cushion.
tissue: To investigate cAMP signalling in P. falciparum blood stages, we therefore generated two transgenic parasite lines designed to allow the conditional disruption of either ACβ or PKAc.
cell_type: we profiled the ACβ- and PKA-dependent phosphoproteomes from parasite cultures comprising mature schizonts and merozoites—the parasite life stages in which cAMP-dependent signalling could plausibly exert control over the invasion process.
sample_source: P. falciparum erythrocytic stages were cultured in human erythrocytes (National Blood Transfusion Service, UK) and RPMI 1640 medium (Life Technologies) supplemented with 0.5% Albumax type II (Gibco), 50 μM hypoxanthine, and 2 mM L-glutamine.
strain: The PKAc-HA:loxP line was generated from the DiCre-expressing 3D7 P. falciparum clone using SLI of a plasmid based on pL7
